output.brief:
The Kestria buffering is almost certainly caused by smart-TV app 5.2, not the new CDN. Version 5.2 lowered the streaming startup buffer from 10 s to 4 s. Kestria was the only market given it, starting 9 Oct, the same day as the CDN cutover. That timing is why the CDN looked guilty. Telemetry shows 5.2 TVs stalling 5.9% of viewing time on every ISP. Every other client in Kestria, on the same CDN and the same ISPs, stays at about 0.7%. Employee test TVs on the old CDN (Corvane) showed the same problem (5.7% on 5.2 vs 0.6% on 5.1) before the cutover. The handball launch and ISP congestion don't fit, because only 5.2 TVs are affected.

Recommendation: don't send the SLA breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back; that would punish the wrong party and wouldn't fix anything. Don't mute the alert. Instead, revert Kestria to the 5.1 streaming settings through the server-side config (about an hour) and stop the 20 Nov wider rollout until it's fixed. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard. Hold off on the cancellation offer: the October cancellations also coincide with the 1 Oct price rise, and the link to buffering is unproven.
